composite

kuhm-POZ-it · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Composite is made up of several distinct parts combined into one.

The police released a composite sketch drawn from four witnesses' descriptions.

Worked Example

The orchestra's send-off video was a composite of clips filmed by parents at twelve different concerts.

One video was built from many distinct recordings combined into a single whole -- when separate parts merge into one thing, that thing is composite.

How composite sits among its neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

combined

combined: joined together from separate parts

blended

blended: mixed from different elements into one

Antonyms

pure

pure: made of only one thing, with nothing added

unmixed

unmixed: kept as a single, separate ingredient

How Strong Is It? — mixed → composite → amalgamated

mixed vs. composite

mixed vs. composite: Mixed just says different things were stirred together -- composite adds that the parts are distinct and combine into one working whole.

amalgamated vs. composite

amalgamated vs. composite: Amalgamated is a heavier, more technical word -- parts fully merged into a single body, often metals or organizations.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — com-

prefix — com-: together (Latin)

root — posite

root — posite: placed, put (from ponere) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Com- ('together') + posite (from posit-, 'placed'): a composite thing is literally 'placed together' -- separate parts set into one whole.

Use the root in a new word: component

Use the root in a new word: component: A single faulty component kept the entire rocket on the launchpad.

Root Check

Word Choice

Composite is usually an adjective -- a composite sketch, score, or material. It can also be a noun for the combined thing itself ('the sketch was a composite of four descriptions'). Either way, the idea is distinct parts merged into one.
